config.description: Designed confirmation that step token padding is not paid at n>1. Straddles a compiled bucket boundary at fixed batch size and near-fixed per-sequence length, so real work moves ~1.6% while padded work doubles. H1 answered this from a natural experiment; this is the randomised version.
config.note_prediction: cost x~1.02 => padding not paid (cost tracks real tokens). cost x~2.0 => padding paid (cost tracks the compiled bucket).
config.note_seq_len: Per-sequence length is near-constant within an edge (128 vs 130) on purpose. Comparing 4x96 against 4x128 would move sequence length by a third, changing attention work materially and destroying the clean prediction that cost is proportional to real tokens.
config.note_single_step: Both edges sit far below max_num_batched_tokens=8192 so the scheduler has no reason to split. Every dispatch records its step count and splits are counted, not averaged over: a split reintroduces exactly the smearing this experiment exists to avoid.
